description: Drama Foundation width tiers — ACARA v9. All strands are capability strands; primary axis is task_contexts throughout.
subject: Drama

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest single context in which the student honestly meets the descriptor's command term. For Foundation Drama, minimum is one mode, one scenario, or one sharing context — the floor is meeting the command term in any setting, not a rich or elaborated one.
width_notes.typical_width: Full descriptor scope as reflected in common elaborations — what a Foundation class that has genuinely engaged with the standard would have done. Includes a range of modes, contexts and scenarios.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment directions that add new task contexts — different modes, different cultural starting points, digital capture, extended imaginative contexts. Wider does not mean harder; it means a broader range of task types.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations are the primary source for typical_width and for identifying appropriate wider directions. First Nations elaborations appear in wider as a default where present.

AC9ADRFC01.minimum_width: Student creates one arts work — dramatic play, puppet sequence, or scene using repurposed materials — in which an identifiable idea is communicated through at least one arts mode.
AC9ADRFC01.typical_width: Students create arts works across multiple modes (voice, movement, objects, puppetry, digital capture) using repurposed materials, props and available technologies; they draw on stories, personal experience and imagination; pieces have a recognisable intent and are sharable with peers.
wider: Students create works in response to cultural stories from their own community or family heritage, using drama to communicate those stories to others
Students use digital devices to record and voice-over their dramatic play, creating a documented arts work
Students devise a chant or dramatic sequence in which a character communicates a health, sustainability or community message
Students use First Nations Australians' storytelling traditions (using resources co-created with First Nations communities) as inspiration for creating dramatic scenarios about connection to place
elaborations: creating arts works in a range of forms to communicate ideas from lived personal or social experiences
creating works in response to inspiration from sources such as play, imagination, observation, literature, artworks from their cultures and communities
manipulating objects, puppets, 2D images and/or available technologies to create or retell stories
devising a chant/rap that a character could use to communicate a health or sustainability message
repurposing materials and objects as starting points for imagining and developing scenes and scenarios
considering characters and situations associated with a story and re-imagining them

AC9ADRFD01.minimum_width: Student engages in purposeful exploratory play with at least one mode (materials, voice, or movement), notices something from that exploration, and makes at least one 'what if?' extension move.
AC9ADRFD01.typical_width: Students explore tactile materials, movement possibilities, vocal qualities and imaginative scenarios; they discover and extend ideas by asking 'What happens next?'; they respond to stories, images and music through different modes; they document steps in their making using drawing or digital images.
wider: Students explore multiple sensory entry points (sound, texture, movement, image) and compare what each reveals about possible ideas
Students respond to music or soundscapes through movement, discovering how mood and rhythm suggest dramatic possibilities
Students improvise movements to explain a process and capture this in a sequence of images, developing early documentation skills
Students use digital devices to capture their exploration — sequencing images to show how an idea developed
elaborations: playing with the tactile qualities of a range of materials and exploring how they feel to develop ideas
imagining how characters in a story might dress or move, and making still or moving images
playing games to develop subject-specific practices; taking on the point of view of a fictional character
responding to emotions in music and using movement to share their response
exploring their speaking and singing voices and discovering ways to use them to communicate ideas and feelings
improvising movements to explain the steps in a process, then capturing images to document it

AC9ADRFE01.minimum_width: Student identifies at least one arts experience from their life and gives a simple reason why that arts work or experience matters to people.
AC9ADRFE01.typical_width: Students identify multiple arts works and experiences across different community contexts (school, home, screen, cultural events); they discuss why arts are created and shared (for celebrations, communication, teaching, expressing feelings); they connect specific arts works to specific purposes.
wider: Students explore arts works and practices from culturally diverse community contexts, identifying how different communities use arts to express identity and shared values
Students listen to First Nations Australians talk about why the arts matter for connecting to people, culture and Country/Place, using resources created or co-created by First Nations Australians
Students investigate how drama and storytelling in their local community (including any First Nations community context) carries cultural knowledge from one generation to another
elaborations: identifying artworks and experiences in their lives, such as songs, dances, drama, animations, computer games or public art
singing songs used for celebrations such as school songs, anthems, sports teams' songs, birthday songs
exploring how illustrations/images in a text help communicate narrative or information
listening to First Nations Australians talk about the importance of the arts for connecting to people, culture and Country/Place

AC9ADRFP01.minimum_width: Student shares an arts work in an informal setting with at least one other person as audience, and can respond to at least one question about their work.
AC9ADRFP01.typical_width: Students share arts works through gallery walks, performance walks, and class sharing events; they talk about their work using simple descriptive language; they respond to teacher questions about themes, processes and features; they act as attentive audience for peers.
wider: Students present retellings of stories to peers using puppets they have made or repurposed objects
Students create a simple introduction or verbal explanation for their work before sharing it
Students use digital devices to record their arts explorations and curate a sequence of images to share with their teacher and class
Students perform movement or drama sequences to other class groups, introducing their work by describing a favourite moment
elaborations: sharing artworks with the class via a 'gallery' or 'performance walk'
talking about ideas, themes, processes and features of the work
presenting retellings of stories to peers through dramatic play using repurposed objects, toys or puppets
sharing work with teacher and responding to questions about the work
performing movement/dance sequences for other groups and introducing the work
using digital devices to record and curate arts explorations
